newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Not all ports join Brazil stevedore strike--unions.
newsitem.headline: Not all ports join Brazil stevedore strike--unions.

text.p: The head of Brazil's Stevedores Federation said he believed all stevedores were participating in a 24-hour strike, but three unions have told Reuters they are not striking or are taking only token action.
"As far as I know, all the ports have participated," Abelardo Fernandes told Reuters by telephone.
But a union official at the port of Recife said that loading and unloading operations at two sugar vessels and two wheat ships docked at the port were continuing normally.
"We are not participating in the strike as we are currently holding negotiations and so the conditions are not right," he said, adding there were no plans for a strike in the future.

In Maceio the president of the local stevedores union said members were not striking as there were no ships in the port. He declined to comment on whether the union would have joined the strike had vessels been docked.

In Paranagua, the country's key soybean and soyproducts port, members of the stevedores union decided last night to only hold a one-hour strike at 1300 local/1600 GMT. Moreover operations at the grains export terminal would not be interrupted during the stoppage.
Stevedores at the country's two largest coffee exporting ports after Santos - Vitoria and Rio de Janeiro - had however supported the federation's call for a strike.

The stoppage is in support of Santos workers who have effectively halted loading and unloading operations since Wednesday morning in protest at a ruling allowing a steel firm to use company workers to load and unload at its private terminal in the port.
Unions argue only registered and qualified stevedores should be allowed to conduct these operations.
There has been no advance in talks with the steel firm, said Fernandes who is participating in the negotiations.
However there was no question of prolonging the stoppage and all striking workers should return to work at 0700 local/1000 GMT Saturday, he added.
